about.title: About
about.intro: I'm a carpenter and computer scientist who builds things — in wood and in code. My work sits at the intersection of traditional craft and modern software engineering, where precision, patience, and a love for good systems apply equally.
about.carpentry.title: Carpentry
about.carpentry.desc: Furniture making, timber framing, and joinery using both hand tools and modern machinery. Each piece designed to last generations.
about.cs.title: Computer Science
about.cs.desc: Full-stack development, systems programming, and software architecture. Building tools that solve real problems in the workshop and beyond.
about.design.title: Design
about.design.desc: Both disciplines demand careful design before execution. Measure twice, cut once — whether in timber or in code.
about.tools.title: Tools
about.tools.desc: Hand planes, chisels, and mallets alongside Node.js, PostgreSQL, and a terminal. The right tool for the right job, always.
about.techNote: This portfolio is built with Node.js + Express + PostgreSQL + Vanilla JS · MVC + Component pattern
projectDetail.brandPara1: The work was approached the way all our work is at Orange Smiley — whether it is a store that has to hold up under December traffic or a database schema built to survive years of production without a rewrite.
projectDetail.brandPara2: The result is a system as usable as it is good-looking, built to last and to hold up under real-world use.

adminBooks.settings.peppolOk: E-invoicing (Peppol BIS 3.0): the seller address is recorded as parts — UBL documents can be emitted.
adminBooks.settings.peppolMissing: E-invoicing (Peppol BIS 3.0) needs the seller's street, postal code, city and country recorded as parts; until then no UBL document can be emitted.
adminBooks.detail.ublNotReady: Cannot be emitted as an e-invoice:
adminBooks.peppol.NOT_ISSUED: The invoice has not been issued (draft or cancelled).
adminBooks.peppol.RECEIPT_SERIES: A till receipt has no addressable buyer — Peppol is business-to-business.
adminBooks.peppol.SELLER_INCOMPLETE: The seller's name, kennitala or VAT number is missing on the invoice.
adminBooks.peppol.SELLER_ADDRESS_INCOMPL: The invoice carries no structured seller address (issued before migration 095, or the parts were not set in the settings at issue). It cannot be derived from the printed text.
adminBooks.peppol.BUYER_ADDRESS_INCOMPLE: The invoice carries no structured buyer address (issued before migration 095, or from an order without one). It cannot be derived from the printed text.
adminBooks.peppol.BUYER_COUNTRY_INVALID: The buyer's country is not a valid two-letter ISO code.
adminBooks.peppol.ZERO_RATE_WITHOUT_REAS: A 0% VAT line without an export reason — 0% on a domestic line is a data error.
adminBooks.peppol.UNSUPPORTED_RATE: A line carries a VAT rate the EN 16931 mapping does not know.
adminBooks.peppol.TOTALS_INCONSISTENT: The sum of the lines does not match the invoice's net amount.
adminBooks.peppol.VAT_ROUNDING_DRIFT: Per-line VAT differs from the EN 16931 per-rate calculation by more than 3 kr. — that is not rounding.
adminBooks.intake.title: Waiting ({count})
adminBooks.intake.hint: A queued document is a PROPOSAL. Nothing is booked until you open it into the entry form, check every figure and save — the document then attaches automatically as the supporting document.
adminBooks.intake.alreadyQueued: The same document is already waiting.
adminBooks.intake.accepting: Booking from the queue — the queued document will be the supporting document. Check every figure before saving.
adminBooks.detail.refundHint: Records money going back out. It does not reverse the sale — use a credit note for that.
adminBooks.detail.confirmRefund: Record this refund? It cannot be deleted, only reversed.
adminBooks.expenses.title: Expenses
adminBooks.expenses.subtitle: Purchases and supplier invoices, with their receipts.
adminBooks.expenses.vatNumberHint: Without a VAT number the input VAT is not deductible.
adminBooks.expenses.amountHintForeign: The amount in {currency} exactly as it appears on the invoice, with two decimals (e.g. 20.00).
adminBooks.expenses.receiptHint: PDF or photo of the invoice. Can be added later.
adminBooks.expenses.uploadedDuplicate: Receipt ready: {name} — an identical file is already on record.
adminBooks.expenses.searchPlaceholder: Search by supplier, invoice number or description
adminBooks.expenses.missingHint: {amount} of input VAT is unsubstantiated. No input VAT is deductible without a receipt.
adminBooks.expenses.verdictReverseCharge: Reverse charge: you self-assess the VAT. Output and input cancel out, but both appear on the return.
adminBooks.ar.title: Receivables
adminBooks.ar.subtitle: Who owes you and for how long, counted from the due date.
adminBooks.ar.guestNote: Customers without an account are grouped by email, so the same person can appear twice if they used two addresses.
adminBooks.ar.tileOverdueHint: This is the amount you should be chasing.
adminBooks.ar.tileWorstHint: The oldest debts — least likely to be collected.
adminBooks.statement.subtitle: Statement of invoices, payments and credit notes
adminBooks.statement.inCredit: The balance is in the customer’s favour — you owe them.
adminBooks.vat.title: VAT returns
adminBooks.vat.subtitle: The VSK return (RSK 10.01), derived from the general ledger.
adminBooks.vat.asFiledHint: These figures are as filed. They do not change even if the books do.
adminBooks.vat.derivedHint: Derived from the posted entries in this period. Updates until the return is filed.
adminBooks.vat.boxAHint: Sales excluding VAT at the standard rate.
adminBooks.vat.boxBHint: Sales excluding VAT at the reduced rate (books, food, etc.).
adminBooks.vat.boxCHint: Exports and other zero-rated sales. Requires evidence.
adminBooks.vat.nothingToReview: Nothing to review. This period is ready to file.
adminBooks.vat.sourcesHint: The accounts behind each box, so an accountant can trace any figure.
adminBooks.vat.fileHint: Filing freezes these figures and locks the period. The settlement entry is posted automatically.
adminBooks.vat.overrideHint: Requires an explanation, which is stored with the return.
adminBooks.vat.confirmFile: File the VAT return for {period} and lock the period? The figures will be frozen.
adminBooks.vat.filedToast: VAT return filed and period locked.
adminBooks.vat.reopenHint: Use this if the return was filed by mistake and has NOT been submitted to Skatturinn. The stored return is deleted and the action is recorded in the audit trail.
adminBooks.vat.confirmReopen: Re-open this period and delete the stored return?
adminBooks.vat.boxDReverse: of which reverse charge (services from abroad)
adminBooks.vat.boxDSplitHint: Reverse-charge VAT is output VAT but NOT domestic turnover — it has its own line on RSK 10.01 and cancels against input VAT.
adminBooks.vat.finding.ALREADY_FILED: A return for this period was already filed on {date}. A filed return cannot be changed — correct it through the next period, or re-open the period if it was not actually submitted.
adminBooks.vat.finding.UNPOSTED_DRAFTS: {count} journal entries are still drafts in this period. Draft entries are not part of the books, so their figures are missing from this return — and once posted they will land in whichever period is open then.
adminBooks.vat.finding.UNSUBSTANTIATED_I: {count} deductible purchases have no receipt attached, claiming {amount} of input VAT that cannot be proven. Attach the receipts, or mark the purchases non-deductible.
adminBooks.vat.finding.UNINVOICED_ORDERS: {count} paid orders have not been invoiced ({amount}). That turnover is missing from this return, and the duty to declare a sale does not wait for the invoice.
adminBooks.vat.finding.SUSPENSE_NOT_EMPT: The suspense account holds {amount}. Those entries have no decided treatment yet, so their VAT may belong on this return.
adminBooks.vat.finding.ZERO_RATED_NEEDS_: Box C reports {amount} of zero-rated turnover. Zero-rating must be supported by evidence of export, or of the customer being a business outside Iceland. Make sure that evidence is on file before filing.
adminBooks.vat.finding.REFUND_POSITION: This period claims a refund of {amount}. That is normal when input VAT exceeds output VAT — check it is what you expect.
adminBooks.vat.finding.NIL_RETURN: No VAT was recorded in this period at all. A nil return is still required, but check nothing is simply unentered.
adminBooks.vat.finding.PAST_DEADLINE: The filing deadline was {due_on}, {days} days ago.
adminBooks.bank.title: Bank reconciliation
adminBooks.bank.subtitle: Prove the books against the bank and card settlements.
adminBooks.bank.importHint: CSV from your online bank. The same statement can be imported more than once — lines already present are skipped.
adminBooks.bank.someLinesSkipped: {count} lines could not be read and were skipped.
adminBooks.bank.stripeHint: Pulls fees and payouts. A card payment lands in the clearing account; the payout moves it to the bank.
adminBooks.bank.ledgerBalanceHint: The bank account according to the general ledger.
adminBooks.bank.reconciled: The books and the bank agree.
adminBooks.bank.notReconciled: Something is in the books that is not at the bank, or the other way round.
adminBooks.bank.clearingHint: Card money Stripe has not paid out yet. Should match Stripe.
adminBooks.bank.noSuggestions: No suggestions — explain the line below.
adminBooks.bank.expenseHint: expense: explain the line against account 2100
adminBooks.ledger.title: General ledger
adminBooks.ledger.subtitle: Every posted entry, and the reports built on them.
adminBooks.ledger.empty: No posted entries in this period.
adminBooks.ledger.unbalanced: The trial balance does not balance — out by {amount}. That is a fault in the ledger itself; do not rely on the other reports until it is resolved.
adminBooks.ledger.bsUnbalanced: The balance sheet does not balance — out by {amount}.
adminBooks.ledger.revenueHint: Excluding VAT — VAT is not revenue.
adminBooks.ledger.profitHint: Revenue less expenses for the period.
adminBooks.ledger.retainedHint: Retained earnings are derived (revenue less expenses to date), not posted — this system has no year-end closing entry. That is what keeps the balance sheet and the profit and loss from ever disagreeing.
adminBooks.ledger.truncated: Too many movements to show — narrow the period or use the CSV export.
adminBooks.ledger.manualHint: For an opening balance, a depreciation charge or an accountant’s adjustment. The entry must balance and the memo is required — a manual entry with no explanation is unreadable a year later.
adminBooks.ledger.memoPlaceholder: What is being posted, and why?
adminBooks.ledger.minLines: An entry needs at least two lines.
adminBooks.ledger.needAccount: Pick an account for every line.
adminBooks.ledger.oneSideOnly: Each line is either a debit or a credit — not both.
adminBooks.ledger.mustBalance: The entry does not balance — out by {amount}.
adminBooks.ledger.reversePrompt: Reverse entry {number}? Nothing is deleted — a mirror entry is posted. Why?
adminBooks.ledger.totalsIdle: Enter debits and credits — they must balance
adminBooks.payroll.title: Payroll
adminBooks.payroll.subtitle: Salaries, withholding tax and what is owed to Skatturinn.
adminBooks.payroll.bandsHint: Each band’s rate is the COMBINED income tax and municipal rate, exactly as Skatturinn publishes it. The municipal rate is not added again — it is shown here for reference only.
adminBooks.payroll.bandsFormHint: The lowest band must start at 0 kr. Enter the combined rate (income tax + municipal), not income tax alone — otherwise withholding comes out short by roughly a third.
adminBooks.payroll.needOneBand: At least one band is required.
adminBooks.payroll.refHint: RSK publishes these minimums every year. An owner who pays themselves below the minimum for their category has it assessed later, with interest.
adminBooks.payroll.noFiguresBody: The tax bands, personal allowance, social security and pension rates are set annually. Enter the year’s figures from Skatturinn’s published table before running payroll.
adminBooks.payroll.unconfirmedBody: Payroll will not compute anything until someone has checked the figures against Skatturinn’s published table. A run on unconfirmed figures produces a plausible amount that is too low — and the shortfall is the employer’s liability, not the employee’s.
adminBooks.payroll.confirmPrompt: Confirm the payroll figures for {year}? Write down where they came from — e.g. “skatturinn.is, checked 4 January”.
adminBooks.payroll.notePrompt: A note on where the figures came from is required.
adminBooks.payroll.yearFormHint: Every figure here is read off Skatturinn’s published table. Rates are entered as percentages (6.35 — not 0.0635).
adminBooks.payroll.saveUnconfirms: Editing the figures clears the confirmation — they need checking again.
adminBooks.payroll.figuresSaved: Figures saved. Confirm them before running payroll.
adminBooks.payroll.owedHint: Read from the ledger, not from the payroll runs — only the books know whether the remittance has actually gone out.
adminBooks.payroll.name: Name
adminBooks.payroll.overrideHint: A blank pension rate means “use the year’s minimum” — which is not the same as 0. A collective agreement may be more generous than the minimum, never less.
adminBooks.payroll.ownerHint: An owner needs a reference wage category, so the minimum salary can be checked.
adminBooks.payroll.draftHint: A draft computes payslips but posts nothing. The tax year comes from the PAY DATE — December’s salary paid in January is taxed on January’s figures.
adminBooks.payroll.draftedWithBlockers: Draft computed, but {count} thing(s) block posting.
adminBooks.payroll.confirmPost: Post the payroll? This creates a liability to Skatturinn and cannot be deleted — only reversed.
adminBooks.payroll.postedOverridden: Payroll posted, with the reason recorded.
adminBooks.payroll.overridePrompt: Post anyway? Write the reason — it is stored with the run.
adminBooks.payroll.reversePrompt: Reverse this payroll run? Nothing is deleted — a mirror entry is posted. Why?
adminBooks.payroll.payPrompt: How much was paid? {amount} is outstanding.
adminBooks.payroll.badAmount: The amount must be a whole number greater than zero.
adminBooks.payroll.employerCost: Total employer cost: {amount} — the gross plus social security and the employer’s pension contribution.
adminBooks.pos.title: Counter sales
adminBooks.pos.subtitle: Over-the-counter sales — receipt, VAT and posting in one go.
adminBooks.pos.productNoRate: {name} has no VAT rate. Set it on the product — the till does not guess.
adminBooks.pos.freeLineHint: For a repair, a delivery charge, or anything that is not a shop product. The VAT rate is required — a till cannot ask.
adminBooks.pos.badPrice: The price must be a whole number greater than zero.
adminBooks.pos.emptyBasket: Nothing on the counter yet. Pick a product to start.
adminBooks.pos.buyerHint: A receipt does not need a name. A business buyer does need their kennitala on it, to deduct the input VAT.
adminBooks.pos.cashHint: {count} sales — this should be in the drawer
adminBooks.pos.cardHint: {count} sales — awaiting settlement from the acquirer
adminBooks.pos.creditedHint: Money that went back out — not netted off the sale, because the sale happened.
adminBooks.pos.vatHint: VAT is extracted from the price, not added to it. Shop prices include VAT.

thjonusta.title: Software for small and medium businesses
thjonusta.intro: Orange Smiley builds the software your business needs. AI does the work alongside us, so you get the solution in weeks, at a price a small business can afford.
thjonusta.servicesIntro: No two businesses are alike. We start from the problem that needs solving, not from a product catalogue.
thjonusta.service.custom.name: Custom systems
thjonusta.service.custom.desc: Systems built around the way you work: orders, bookings, job costing, inventory, internal tools and customer portals. You should not have to bend the business to fit the software.
thjonusta.service.web.name: Websites and online stores
thjonusta.service.web.desc: Fast, secure websites in Icelandic and English, with an online store, payments and content management your staff can handle.
thjonusta.service.integrations.name: Integrations
thjonusta.service.integrations.desc: The systems you already use made to talk to each other, such as accounting, payment gateways and suppliers, so the same data is never typed in twice.
thjonusta.service.automation.name: Automation and AI
thjonusta.service.automation.desc: Repetitive manual work taken off the table: invoice intake, reports, enquiry triage and overviews that keep themselves up to date.
thjonusta.service.migration.name: Moving off legacy systems
thjonusta.service.migration.desc: Data and workflows moved off online store platforms, ageing bespoke systems or spreadsheets without the business stopping.
thjonusta.service.operations.name: Hosting and maintenance
thjonusta.service.operations.desc: We host, monitor and update what we build, and change requests are handled in days.
thjonusta.step1Desc: We learn how the business runs and scope the work with you. The first conversation costs nothing.
thjonusta.step2Desc: A fixed price for the work, never hourly billing. You see and test the system as it takes shape.
thjonusta.step3Desc: One monthly fee covering hosting, monitoring, updates and changes.
thjonusta.productIntro: If you run a store or a wholesale business, you do not have to start from scratch. Rekstrarkerfið is our first product: website, store, inventory and invoicing in one Icelandic system, with custom modules fitted to each business.
thjonusta.productCore: Everyone gets the same solid core, and the features your business needs are built on top of it and kept maintained.
thjonusta.ctaText: An idea, a problem or a system that has seen better days. Describe it and we reply within one working day.
umOkkur.title: Small studio. Big output.
umOkkur.lead: Orange Smiley ehf. is an Icelandic software company that builds and operates websites, online stores and business systems for small and medium businesses.
umOkkur.story1: The company is run by a single founder assisted by AI agents — which means the output of a large studio at a price small businesses can afford. The system you buy is the same system we run ourselves.
umOkkur.story2: Instead of selling hours we sell a subscription: one flat monthly fee covering hosting, monitoring, security updates and changes. Change requests are handled in days, not months.
umOkkur.story3: Our first customer is an Icelandic wholesaler that moved off Shopify onto our platform — see the projects page for the full case study when it opens.
